name: Symphony Ltd
title: Symphony Ltd - 517385 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Symphony's Q4 consol revenue fell to ₹338 crore from ₹488 crore and FY26 PAT was negative ₹141 crore after a ₹259 crore Australia impairment, while standalone gross margin held near 45%+ and management says it will stop funding Australia.

summary.headline: Symphony FY26 consol revenue fell 28% to ₹1,131 crores; Australia fully impaired, taking PAT to negative ₹141 crores.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue fell 28% YoY to ₹1,131 crores and PBT before exceptional items fell to ₹149 crores from ₹326 crores, with PAT at negative ₹141 crores after a ₹259 crores consolidated impairment. Q4 consolidated revenue was ₹338 crores (vs ₹488 crores) and EBITDA margin fell to 15.5% from 21.2%, while gross margin held at 46.4%. Management completed a balance-sheet reset: the entire ₹348 crores Australia equity investment is impaired, no further capital will go to Australia, and the US business and Bonaire IPRs were bought into Symphony India for about ₹52 crores. Standalone Q4 revenue was ₹199 crores (vs ₹368 crores) on a high base and channel caution, with management pointing to a possible 4 to 6 week summer runway from mid-May.

segments.name: Symphony India (standalone)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹765 crores, Q4 revenue ₹199 crores; standalone Q4 gross margin about 45%+ (down ~3 points) and EBITDA margin about 17% vs ~27% a year earlier. Standalone ROCE 149% on ₹78 crores capital employed.

segments.name: Beyond India Summer Products (BISP)
segments.commentary: Includes large space ventilated coolers, tower fans, kitchen fans, water heaters and exports; ₹558 crores of FY26 consolidated sales (~49%). India BISP revenue ₹192 crores, about 25% of standalone; EBITDA in high single-digit % per management.

segments.name: IMPCO Mexico
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹182 crores, EBITDA ₹21 crores, PAT ₹6 crores; flattish revenue with channel inventory overhang.

segments.name: GSK China
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹96 crores, EBITDA ₹8 crores, PAT ₹3 crores before exceptional items (₹49 crores after); repaid ₹26 crores of loan, net outstanding now ₹4 crores vs peak above ₹60 crores.

segments.name: US business
segments.commentary: FY26 sales about ₹45 crores vs ₹30–140 crores range over last five years; mainly air coolers, sourced from India and Mexico; now a direct subsidiary of Symphony India.

segments.name: Climate Technologies Australia
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹182 crores, PAT negative ₹11 crores before exceptional items; losses of ₹60 crores over two years incl. ₹33 crores in FY26. Equity of ₹348 crores fully impaired; ₹165 crores infused in March 2026 to repay loans.

segments.name: Symphony Brazil
segments.commentary: PAT negative ₹3 crores in FY26; operates on a lean outsourced model that management is replicating for Australia.

guidance_outlook: Management expects standalone summer sales to improve if normal summer sets in from the current week; a 4 to 6 week decent-sales runway is cited, but no growth percentage was guided.

Q1 FY27 (June quarter) gross margin impact from PVC and other cost increases expected to be limited (a few points at most) due to lower-cost old inventory; full price pass-through expected from 1 July as new production starts.
No share buyback currently; board to consider at the right time, subject to regulation.
Australia to move to a distributor model with a lean team (CODB ~₹5–6 lakh per month, to fall further after warehousing exits); no closure or sale under consideration.
Subsidiaries (Mexico, China, Brazil) expected to be incrementally profitable and capital-accretive; GSK China's remaining ₹4 crores loan expected to be repaid within six months.
₹52 crores to be remitted from Symphony India treasury in the coming week or two to repay the Australia working-capital loan guaranteed by Symphony India.
capex_capacity: No further capital investment or allocation to Australia business; board categorically decided this, with all Australia commitments treated as complete.
Bonaire USA equity acquired by Symphony India at ~₹30 crores; Bonaire brand IPRs acquired for ~₹23 crores (total ~₹52 crores).
Management referenced 'fully new production' starting 1 July, which will be used to pass through input cost increases.
Australia integrated manufacturing facility already converted to an outsourced model; overheads reduced to less than half of prior levels.
Water heater category launched in FY26 in limited markets; geographic spread to widen in FY27; revenue described as not yet material.
demand_pricing: Q4 standalone revenue decline attributed to high base (March 2025 boosted by unbilled advances), channel caution from inventory overhang, and a poor 2025 summer; South, West and part of Central India saw decent April sales, while North and East channel inventory is largely rationalised.
Weather disturbances continued into April; export revenue hit by Middle East geopolitical headwinds.
Consolidated gross margin held at ~46% despite cost and summer disruption; no pricing pressure per management.
Competition: management says Symphony is a mass-premium brand and that competitors price below it; it defends share with the widest range across value and premium price points.

Air cooler vs AC: management says an air cooler costs about one-third of an AC and offers over 90% power savings, with a 1–2 year payback; cited price ratio of about 30–40 against 100 for lower-end branded AC.
US tariff on Indian product is down to ~12% and Mexico-sourced product carries no tariff; management views the tariff as a non-issue at present.

qa_highlights.question: Is North India weak, and can growth reach double digits in the coming summer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said North and East channel inventory is largely cleared and a decent uptick in April fresh business was seen; it declined to forecast growth until weather visibility improves for 2 to 3 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the US business and its loan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 US sales were about ₹45 crores against a ₹30–140 crores range over five years; EBITDA margin is said to be in line with the domestic business. Australia is the entity where loans were repaid.

qa_highlights.question: What is the future for Climate Technologies Australia and how can it run without funding?
qa_highlights.answer: The business will move to distributors who buy stock from India/China; only a small team and office will remain, with CODB of about ₹5–6 lakh per month. Closure or sale is not being considered.

qa_highlights.question: Subsidiary-wise sales, EBITDA and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: IMPCO Mexico revenue ₹182 crores, EBITDA ₹21 crores, PAT ₹6 crores; GSK China revenue ₹96 crores, EBITDA ₹8 crores, PAT ₹3 crores before exceptional; Symphony Brazil PAT negative ₹3 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin of BISP versus the air cooler business?
qa_highlights.answer: BISP EBITDA is in the high single-digit range even after heavy advertising and launch costs; large space ventilated coolers now exceed the residential air cooler margin. Standalone EBITDA margin is 17% against 27% last year.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company passing on PVC and other cost increases?
qa_highlights.answer: The June quarter benefits from low-cost old inventory, with a few points of gross margin impact at most; full price pass-through is expected from 1 July as new production starts.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company do a share buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: No buyback now; the board will consider one at the right time, subject to regulation. The last buyback was in 2024.

risks_watch: Summer weather: whether the expected 4 to 6 week selling window materialises, especially in North and East India; April was disrupted.
Input cost inflation (PVC and others) and whether price increases fully pass through from 1 July without volume loss.
Standalone EBITDA margin compression (17% vs 27%) from weak operating leverage, and high advertising and launch costs in BISP.
Residual Australia exposure: ₹52 crores IPR and US purchase, ₹52 crores treasury outflow to repay the guaranteed working-capital loan, and the distributor-model transition.
Export headwinds from Middle East geopolitics; IMPCO Mexico channel inventory overhang.
summary.management_tone: Candid and conciliatory on Australia, which management openly calls a failed acquisition thesis, with a firm 'nothing more to lose' stance. Confident on gross margin and the BISP and subsidiary story, but evasive on quarterly growth, buybacks and standalone volume recovery, which were deferred to weather visibility.
key_quotes: So, all put together, the impairment is ₹259 crores, including goodwill is some of the intangible assets and deferred tax.
And at the cost of repetition, nothing more to impair or in other words, nothing more to lose.
The Board of Directors and company has very importantly and categorically decided that no further capital investment or allocation will be made to Australia business.
Nrupesh Shah: So no share buyback as of now.
So, whatever we were to invest, whatever we were to commit, we have done enough.
But as fully new production takes place and starting 1st July, we will be in a position to pass entire price increase in one way or other way.

growth.why: No revenue growth % guided; management cites a 4-6 week summer sales runway and full price pass-through from 1 July, but no volume or growth target and no specific capacity or order numbers back it, while Q4 consolidated revenue fell about 31% (₹338 cr vs ₹488 cr) and standalone fell about 46%.
